events.title: 📓 DIY Digital Notebook Workshop
events.venue: Iffy Books, 404 S. 20th St., Philadelphia, 19146, United States
events.description:
In this workshop you’ll build a digital notebook, a pocket-sized device for taking notes with a USB keyboard. We’re using affordable, widely available components: a Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 microcontroller, a 1-inch OLED display, and a microSD card reader, arranged on a solderless breadboard. The ESP32-S3 connects to the display via the I2C (Inter-Integrated Circuit) protocol, and to the microSD card reader uses the SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) protocol. 
No soldering required! Cutting and stripping jumper wires requires a degree of manual dexterity. 
Please bring a laptop if you have one! If not it’s OK.

events.title: 🔋 Beginner Soldering: Li-Ion Battery Pack
events.venue: Iffy Books, 404 S. 20th St., Philadelphia, 19146, United States
events.description:
Make a rechargeable battery pack for your LoRa node, a microcontroller such as an ESP32 or Pi Pico, or anything that runs on 3–4 Volts. Perfect for folks who’ve never soldered before! 
To complete this project you’ll need to buy a li-ion battery pack kit for $3.99. Here’s what it includes: 
• 18650 battery clip w/ attached wires
• TP4056 charge controller board
• PH2.5 plug w/ attached wires
• 1/8″ heat shrink tubing (1.5″ long)
• 1/2″ heat shrink tubing (1″ long) 
You’ll also need a lithium-ion 18650 battery, available separately.

If you’re joining for the first time, I’d suggest you read this before anything else for brief context: What the Luddites Really Fought Against by Richard Conniff.The only expectation is that you read the chapter(s) of the book that’s listed for that meeting. You’re still welcome to participate if you haven’t done the readings as long as you are mindful. events.description:
In this workshop you’ll build a device that displays your GPS coordinates and the current time, without connecting to the internet or transmitting anything. 100% passive and off-grid, no internet or cell connection needed!

rubber band (to attach GPS antenna to breadboard)

events.title: 🔊 DJ Basixxx with Mixxx
events.venue: Iffy Books, 404 S. 20th St., Philadelphia, 19146, United States
events.description:
If you’re curious about DJing but don’t have money to drop on equipment, this workshop is for you! You’ll learn to use Mixxx, a free and open source DJ program for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Mixxx supports a wide range of DJ controller hardware, but to make it more accessible we’re using regular QWERTY keyboards with stickers on the important keys. We’ll teach you to find tracks on the web, load them into Mixxx, and get started with beatmatching. It’s easier then you think! 
You’ll need to bring your own laptop and headphones for this workshop. We also recommend bringing a separate USB keyboard if you have one, ideally with a row of function keys (F1, F2, F3, etc.). If you have an external audio interface, you’re welcome to bring that too. 
The DJ controller sticker sheets we’re using are available on our online store. Or print your own (4″ x 4″) on sticker paper!
